title: The Horse and the Overloaded Ass
text:
A man set out on a journey with a horse and an ass. He put the whole load on the ass, and the horse trotted along carrying nothing at all.

The ass struggled under the weight. After a while he begged the horse to take part of the load. It would be nothing much for you, he said, and it might save my life. The horse refused. The load was not his business, and he had no intention of tiring himself.

The ass staggered on a little farther, then collapsed on the road and died. Their master did not leave the goods behind. He moved the entire load onto the horse, and on top of it he added the skin of the dead ass.

The horse groaned under the burden. Now he understood. He had refused to carry a small share when it was offered, and as a result he was carrying all of it, and the hide of his companion besides.
lesson: Helping a struggling colleague with part of the load is often cheaper than refusing. When one member of a team breaks down, the work falls on those who are left.
people: A horse, an ass, their master
source: Aesop's Fables, The Horse and the Loaded Ass (Perry 181)
